records.subject: Demand for direct international flights from Tirupati to Dubai and Abu Dhabi.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Meda Raghunadha Reddy: I draw attention of the Government to the need for commencing direct international flight services from Tirupati Airport to Dubai and Abu Dhabi, which are major global aviation hubs providing seamless onward connectivity to Europe and the United States of America.A substantial number of residents from Annamayya, YSR Kadapa, Nellore, Ananthapur and Chittoor districts of Andhra Pradeshare employed in Gulf, Europe and Western countries. Many passengers from this region travel frequently for employment, higher education, business and family purposes. Due to the absence of direct international connectivity from Tirupati, passengers have to travel to Chennai, Bengaluru or Hyderabad to board international flights. This causes avoidable financial burden, longer transit time and physical hardship, particularly for senior citizens, women, and children. Tirupati is one of the most important spiritual destinations in the country, being the gateway to Tirumala. Direct international flights from Tirupati would greatly facilitate NRIs residing in Gulf and Western countries to directly visit Tirumala for Darshan, without multiple domestic transits. Considering the large expatriate population from the Rayalaseema region, growing international passenger demand and strategic importance of Dubai and Abu Dhabi as global transit hubs, there is a strong and compelling case for initiating direct international flights from Tirupati. I therefore urge the Government for initiating necessary steps in coordination with airlines and airport authorities, to operationalize direct international flight services from Tirupati to Dubai and Abu Dhabi at the earliest, in the interest of passengers and regional development.

(ENDS)

records.subject: EXPANSION OF NUCLEAR POWER CAPACITY
records.extent:
17 nuclear power reactors with a total capacity of 13100 MW are under implementation, comprising of 7
nuclear reactors under construction and 10 reactors under pre-project activities. These are
expected to be completed progressively by 2031-32.
The details of 17 reactors under implementation are as
follows:
rojects under Construction / Commissioning

Rawatbhata (Rajasthan) – RAPP-8: 1×700 MW (98.60%)

Kudankulam (Tamil Nadu) – KKNPP-3&4: 2×1000 MW (80.51%)

Kudankulam (Tamil Nadu) – KKNPP-5&6: 2×1000 MW (41.56%)

Gorakhpur (Haryana) – GHAVP-1&2: 2×700 MW (Civil works in progress)

Projects under Pre-Project Activities

Kaiga (Karnataka) – Kaiga-5&6: 2×700 MW

Gorakhpur (Haryana) – GHAVP-3&4: 2×700 MW

Chutka (Madhya Pradesh) – Chutka-1&2: 2×700 MW

Mahi Banswara (Rajasthan) – Units 1–4: 4×700 MW

records.subject: RARE EARTH MINERALS
records.extent:
The Union Cabinet has approved the scheme to promote manufacturing of Sintered
Rare Earth Permanent Magnet (REPM) with financial outlay of Rs. 7,280 Crore on
26th November, 2025, to establish 6,000 metric tonnes per annum (MTPA) of
integrated REPM manufacturing capacity in the country. Five beneficiaries are
envisaged under the scheme through global competitive bidding. A transparent Least
Cost System (LCS), comprising a two-envelope process i.e. technical bid and
financial bid is envisaged.
